newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Kabila names incomplete cabinet in ex-Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Kabila names incomplete cabinet in ex-Zaire.

text.p: Laurent Kabila, self-proclaimed president of the former Zaire, named an incomplete government on Thursday night after five hours of closed-door talks, leaving the prime minister's job vacant.
Hours behind a scheduled announcement of the transitional government, newly-appointed Information Minister Raphael Ghenda went on state radio just before midnight to read out a list of 13 ministers.

There was no mention of veteran opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi. Kabila, whose rebels took over Africa's third largest country on May 17, is under domestic and foreign pressure to appoint Tshisekedi prime minister -- one of the posts not announced on Thursday night.
"The complete list of ministers will be known shortly," a statement signed by Kabila and read by Ghenda said.

The key Foreign, Interior, Finance and Mines ministries were all given to members of Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL). No defence minister was named in the initial list.
Analysts said the incomplete cabinet indicated a failure so far to agree terms with Tshisekedi, the popular politician who had led non-violent opposition to President Mobutu Sese Seko since 1980.
Mobutu went into exile last weekend as Kabila's forces entered Kinshasa, crowning a seven-month rebellion with victory.
Kabila arrived in the teeming capital on Tuesday night and 48 hours later had still not appeared in public or addressed his nation of 40 million people.

Alliance sources reported lively debate about the cabinet between the Alliance's executive comittee at Thursday's talks inside the prime minister's official residence, where Kabila has set up his closely guarded headquarters.
State radio broke into a programme of classical music to broadcast the partial cabinet list.
